title: Tensor-unit normalization of derived Hom sections
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its module derived category D [def-pc-derived-category], tensor unit 1 and tensor product [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure], internal Hom H [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and zeroth hypercohomology Q [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. Let q(A,K,L):Hom(A,H(K,L)) ≃ Hom(A tensor K,L) satisfy IsCanonicalDerivedTensorHom [def-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-hom-bijection]. There exist additive equivalences gamma(A):Q(A) ≃ Hom(1,A) natural covariantly in A, and e(P):Q(H(P)) ≃ Hom(P1,P2) natural on D^op times D. Their naturality equations are gamma(B)(Q(f)(x))=gamma(A)(x);f and e(P-prime)(Q(H(f))(x))=unop(f1);e(P)(x);f2. For every K,L and x in Q(H(K,L)), e(K,L)(x)=lambda_K^{-1};q(1,K,L)(gamma(H(K,L))(x)). No scheme morphism, pullback functor, direct image or adjunction is involved.

source.place: Tags 08DJ (lemma-internal-hom) and 08JA (global Hom identification); representative identification in original parent proof step 2, specialized to the tensor unit. Checked at the official Stacks tag pages.

proof.text: Naturality of q in its first variable expresses q(A,K,L)(f) as (f tensor identity);q(H(K,L),K,L)(identity). The shared derived tensor is additive in each variable, so this formula proves q preserves addition. Its given bijection therefore upgrades to an additive equivalence (private qAdd).

For K=unit, precomposition with the inverse right unitor defines unitHom(A,B):Hom(A,H(unit,B)) equiv Hom(A,B). Naturality of q and of the right unitor prove naturality of unitHom in both variables (unitHom_left and unitHom_right). Define B -> H(unit,B) as unitHom(B,B) inverse applied to identity_B, and H(unit,B) -> B as unitHom(H(unit,B),B) applied to identity. The two naturality equations prove the inverse identities and naturality of this explicit unitIso. There is no selection from an existence theorem.

Take a natural additive global-Hom family e0 from rhom_global_sections. Apply Q to unitIso(B), obtaining an additive equivalence Q(B) equiv Q(H(unit,B)), and follow it by e0(unit,B). This constructs gamma(B):Q(B) equiv Hom(unit,B). Naturality of unitIso and of e0 proves naturality of gamma. This uses the stated existential naturality, not naturality of an arbitrary family.

Define e(K,L) as gamma(H(K,L)), followed by qAdd(unit,K,L), followed by precomposition with the inverse left unitor. This is an additive equivalence and satisfies the normalization equation by its definition. Naturality of gamma moves the Q(H(f)) input to composition by H(f). The given naturality of q then gives (identity tensor unop(f1));q(gamma(x));f2. Naturality of the inverse left unitor turns this into unop(f1);e(K,L)(x);f2. These constructions and equations are fully proved in sectionsUnitReduction. Specialize to the derived module category, installing its existing MonoidalPreadditive structure; the representative half of the canonical predicate is unused.

proof_origin.note: Fully proved categorical construction from the existing natural rhom_global_sections family. Naturality of tensor-Hom supplies the unit internal-Hom isomorphism and additive uncurrying; no representative compatibility hole is introduced. Source results 08JA and 08DJ read at the official Stacks pages.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_derivedTensorHom_sections_unit (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    (q : ∀ A K L : schemeDerivedCategory X,
      (A ⟶ (derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
        X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op K, L)) ≃ (A ⊗ K ⟶ L))
    (hq : IsCanonicalDerivedTensorHom X q) :
    ∃ (γ : ∀ A : schemeDerivedCategory X,
        (ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj A ≃+ (𝟙_ (schemeDerivedCategory X) ⟶ A))
      (e : ∀ P : (schemeDerivedCategory X)ᵒᵖ × schemeDerivedCategory X,
        (ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
          ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj P) ≃+ (P.1.unop ⟶ P.2)),
      (∀ (A B : schemeDerivedCategory X) (f : A ⟶ B)
          (x : (ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj A),
        γ B ((ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map f x) = γ A x ≫ f) ∧
      (∀ (P P' : (schemeDerivedCategory X)ᵒᵖ × schemeDerivedCategory X) (f : P ⟶ P')
          (x : (ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
              ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
                X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj P)),
        e P' ((ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map
            ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
              X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).map f) x) = f.1.unop ≫ e P x ≫ f.2) ∧
      (∀ (K L : schemeDerivedCategory X)
          (x : (ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj
              ((derivedInternalHom (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
                X.toRingedSpace.sheaf).obj (op K, L))),
        e (op K, L) x = (λ_ K).inv ≫ q _ K L (γ _ x))
